This guide walks through understanding instant navigations, writing a route that navigates instantly, visualizing what's in the initial UI, and locking the behavior in with end-to-end tests.

## What "instant" means

A navigation is **instant** when the browser can start rendering the new page the moment the user clicks, with static, cached, and fallback content showing up right away, while the server streams the remaining content into its fallbacks.

> **Good to know:** This definition assumes caches are warm. Cold caches still require the server to compute the cached result once, so the first navigation to a route may still wait.

A direct visit and a client navigation to the same route can produce different initial UI. **Direct visits** get the [**static shell**](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell) as HTML, typically from a CDN. **Client navigations** only re-render below the layout the current and destination routes share, so the fallback UI defined by a `<Suspense>` boundary above that point can't be used during the transition.

Whether the new page appears instantly depends on the `<Suspense>` boundaries and caching present below the shared layout.

<details>
<summary>Why page loads and client navigations produce different initial UI</summary>

On a page load, the entire page renders from the document root. Every component runs on the server, and anything that suspends is caught by the nearest `<Suspense>` boundary in the full tree.

The fix is usually to cache the data with `use cache` or wrap it in a `` boundary. 686 687 ## How `instant` differs from `ensureStatic` 688 689 `instant` validates whether a navigation shows UI immediately. [`ensureStatic`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/ensureStatic) requires selected server-rendered output to be static instead of rendered for each request. A route can be fully static and still block a navigation, for example when a Client Component loads data in the browser. 690 691 ## Configuring validation defaults 692 693 By default (`validationLevel: 'warning'`), Cache Components apps validate every Page and Default segment in development. The `experimental.instantInsights.validationLevel` config tunes this behavior — for example, to limit validation to segments that opt in explicitly via `instant`. 694 695 ```js filename="next.config.js" 696 module.exports = { 697 experimental: { 698 instantInsights: { 699 validationLevel: 'warning', 700 }, 701 }, 702 } 703 ``` 704 705 The supported levels are: 706 707 - **`'warning'`** _(framework default)_: Every Page and Default segment is implicitly validated at warning level (dev only). 708 - **`'manual-warning'`**: Only segments with an explicit `instant` are validated, at warning level (dev only). 709 710 Setting `instant = false` on a segment opts it out of validation entirely. 711 712 > **Good to know**: 713 > 714 > - The framework default may change in future versions to opt users into higher levels of validation. Because this feature is experimental, that change is not considered a breaking change. To pin a specific behavior, set `validationLevel` explicitly. 715 > - Framework-synthesized error routes (`/_global-error`, `/_not-found`) are excluded from implicit validation. To validate them, opt in explicitly with `instant`. 716 717 ## Inspecting loading states 718 719 The Navigation Inspector is available when Cache Components is enabled: 720 721 ```js filename="next.config.js" 722 module.exports = { 723 cacheComponents: true, 724 } 725 ``` 726 727 Open the Next.js DevTools and select **Navigation Inspector**, then turn on **Pause on navigations**. While the toggle is on: 728 729 - Refresh the page to freeze the initial static UI generated for the route, before any dynamic data streams in. 730 - Click a link to freeze the prefetched UI for the destination route. 731 732 When the UI is frozen, click **Resume** to let the current navigation finish. The toggle stays on, so the next refresh or link click pauses too. Turn it off when you are done. Use both page refreshes and link clicks to check that your loading states look right on first visit and on navigation. 733 734 ## Testing instant navigation 735 736 The `@next/playwright` package exports an `instant()` helper that holds back dynamic content while the callback runs against the instant UI. The testing API is available automatically in development. For a production build, enable [`experimental.exposeTestingApiInProductionBuild`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/exposeTestingApiInProductionBuild) in the test build. See the [guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) for a full example. 737 738 ```typescript 739 import { instant } from '@next/playwright' 740 ``` 741 742 {/* TODO: remove when fixed and from prod-docs-release */} 743 744 ## Known issue: shared cookie across projects 745 746 The DevTools use a `next-instant-navigation-testing` cookie to hold back dynamic content and freeze the page at the instant UI. Because cookies are scoped to the domain and not the port, running multiple projects on the same domain (typically `localhost`) means the cookie is shared across them and can cause unexpected behavior. Clear the cookie or close the Navigation Inspector panel when switching between projects to avoid issues. 747 748 > **Good to know:** This will be fixed as part of stabilizing the feature. 749 750 ## TypeScript 751 752 ```tsx 753 type InstantConfig = 754 | true 755 | false 756 | { 757 level?: 'warning' 758 } 759 760 export const instant: InstantConfig = true 761 ``` 762 763 ## Version History 764 765 | Version | Changes | 766 | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 767 | `v16.3.0` | `instant` export stabilized, replacing `unstable_instant` (Cache Components only). | 768

The product title now shows up right away, and the live inventory streams in a moment later. **Why it was slow:** `ProductPage` waited on `getInventory()` at the top of the page. That function calls `connection()`, which makes it run fresh on every request, so the whole page waited for it. Clicking the link from home sat on the old page until the inventory came back. **The fix (`app/product/page.tsx`):** - The page itself no longer waits on anything. The `

Premium Widget

` is now part of the page that Next.js builds ahead of time. - The stock count and price moved into a separate `Inventory` component inside a `` boundary. Until the data arrives it shows "Checking availability...", then the real values replace it. - I added `export const instant = true`. This asks Next.js to warn you during development if a later change makes this page wait on data again. **Checked:** `next build` passes and now lists `/product` as a partial prerender (built ahead of time, with live parts streamed in). On a production server, the HTML for `/product` arrives with the title and the "Checking availability..." placeholder, then the stock count. Inventory is still loaded fresh on every request; nothing about it is cached. The build had rewritten `tsconfig.json` and created `.next/` and `next-env.d.ts`. I undid those changes, so the only file I changed is the product page. The edits already in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` were there before I started.
